title: The queen in a busy position
outcomes: Names the piece on a given square before using its rule, with no hint in the prompt
Taps every square a queen can reach by tracing its eight lines separately
Says that the queen does not jump like a knight
Says that a blocker on one line does not stop the queen on the other lines

steps.text: In **How the queen moves** you were told "queen". Now nobody says it. Name the piece first. Then trace its **eight lines** one by one: four along ranks and files, four along diagonals. Each line stops before an own piece, or on the first enemy piece, which can be taken.

steps.caption: The piece on c3 is a queen. Its pawn on e3 and king on e1 stop two lines one square early. The knight on d5 is on none of its lines.

line.say: The queen slides up-left along the diagonal to a5.

steps.text: The queen moves as a rook and a bishop together. Each of the eight lines is blocked on its own: an own piece ends it one square early, and an enemy piece is the last square. A blocker on one line leaves the other seven untouched. *Rule of thumb:* count the lines you traced; eight, even if some are empty.

steps.title: Lines, jumps, blockers
steps.prompt: Predict first. The first position asks for every square. The second asks one yes/no question about a square a knight could reach from the same square. In the third, a pawn moved next to the queen: which of the queen's other lines are still open?
In the silent items, did you trace all eight lines, or did you stop once you had a long list? Which line did you check last?
